# October Weather in Tateyama Japan

Daily high temperatures _decrease_ by _8°F_, from _75°F_ to _68°F_, rarely falling below _62°F_ or exceeding _81°F_.

Daily low temperatures _decrease_ by _9°F_, from _65°F_ to _56°F_, rarely falling below _49°F_ or exceeding _71°F_.

For reference, on _August 9_, the _hottest day_ of the year, temperatures in Tateyama typically range from _75°F_ to _85°F_, while on _January 23_, the _coldest day_ of the year, they range from _38°F_ to _50°F_.

## [Clouds](https://weatherspark.com/m/143796/10/Average-Weather-in-October-in-Tateyama-Japan\#Sections-Clouds)

The month of October in Tateyama experiences _rapidly decreasing_ cloud cover, with the percentage of time that the sky is _overcast_ or _mostly cloudy_ decreasing from _49%_ to _37%_.

The clearest day of the month is _October 31_, with _clear_, _mostly clear_, or _partly cloudy_ conditions _63%_ of the time.

For reference, on _June 27_, the _cloudiest day_ of the year, the chance of overcast or mostly cloudy conditions is _75%_, while on _December 19_, the _clearest day_ of the year, the chance of clear, mostly clear, or partly cloudy skies is _75%_.

## [Humidity](https://weatherspark.com/m/143796/10/Average-Weather-in-October-in-Tateyama-Japan\#Sections-Humidity)

We base the humidity comfort level on the dew point, as it determines whether perspiration will evaporate from the skin, thereby cooling the body. Lower dew points feel drier and higher dew points feel more humid. Unlike temperature, which typically varies significantly between night and day, dew point tends to change more slowly, so while the temperature may drop at night, a muggy day is typically followed by a muggy night.

The chance that a given day will be _muggy_ in Tateyama is _very rapidly decreasing_ during October, _falling_ from _37%_ to _4%_ over the course of the month.

For reference, on _August 7_, the _muggiest day_ of the year, there are muggy conditions _96%_ of the time, while on _January 7_, the _least muggy day_ of the year, there are muggy conditions _0%_ of the time.

## [Data Sources](https://weatherspark.com/m/143796/10/Average-Weather-in-October-in-Tateyama-Japan\#Sections-Sources)

This report illustrates the typical weather in Tateyama, based on a statistical analysis of historical hourly weather reports and model reconstructions from January 1, 1980 to December 31, 2016.

### Temperature and Dew Point

There is only a single weather station, [Tateyama Ab](https://weatherspark.com/y/149403/Average-Weather-at-Tateyama-Ab-Japan-Year-Round), in our network suitable to be used as a proxy for the historical temperature and dew point records of Tateyama.

At a distance of 3 kilometers from Tateyama, closer than our threshold of 150 kilometers, this station is deemed sufficiently nearby to be relied upon as our primary source for temperature and dew point records.

The station records are corrected for the elevation difference between the station and Tateyama according to the [International Standard Atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Standard_Atmosphere), and by the relative change present in the [MERRA-2 satellite-era reanalysis](https://gmao.gsfc.nasa.gov/reanalysis/MERRA-2/) between the two locations.

Please note that the station records themselves may additionally have been back-filled using other nearby stations or the MERRA-2 reanalysis.

### Other Data

All data relating to the Sun's position (e.g., sunrise and sunset) are computed using astronomical formulas from the book, [Astronomical Algorithms 2nd Edition](https://www.amazon.com/Astronomical-Algorithms-Jean-Meeus/dp/0943396611), by Jean Meeus.

All other weather data, including cloud cover, precipitation, wind speed and direction, and solar flux, come from NASA's [MERRA-2 Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis](https://gmao.gsfc.nasa.gov/reanalysis/MERRA-2/). This reanalysis combines a variety of wide-area measurements in a state-of-the-art global meteorological model to reconstruct the hourly history of weather throughout the world on a 50-kilometer grid.

Land Use data comes from the [Global Land Cover SHARE database](http://www.fao.org/land-water/land/land-governance/land-resources-planning-toolbox/category/details/en/c/1036355/), published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

Elevation data comes from the [Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM)](http://www2.jpl.nasa.gov/srtm/), published by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

Names, locations, and time zones of places and some airports come from the [GeoNames Geographical Database](http://www.geonames.org/).

Time zones for airports and weather stations are provided by [AskGeo.com](https://askgeo.com/).

## Weather in the Tateyama Kurobe Area

The **Tateyama Kurobe** area is located at the border of Toyama and Nagano Prefectures, situated within the high-altitude Northern Alps.

As a result, the region experiences distinct seasons with significant climate variations depending on mountain altitude. Precipitation is abundant year-round, especially with deep snow during winter, making it one of Japan’s renowned heavy snowfall regions.

The summer climate is cool and refreshing, perfect for escaping the heat; spring and autumn are ideal times to enjoy flowers and fall foliage; winter, from November to April, transforms the area into a snow-covered winter wonderland.

Below, we provide an overview of the temperature, clothing recommendations, and precautions for each season, helping visitors better adapt to the unique climate of the Tateyama Kurobe region.

## 2026 Opening Dates for Tateyama Kurobe

One of the main attractions in the Tateyama Kurobe area is the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route,” a world-famous mountain sightseeing route that is accessible only during certain periods of the year due to heavy snow blocking access in winter.

The 2026 opening period is from April 15 to November 30.

Following the opening of the route each year, visitors can enjoy the breathtaking Snow Wall (height approximately 15 to 20 meters), a spectacular sight that is usually accessible until late June.

The [Alpen Route official website](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/) updates the latest conditions daily, including snow wall height and whether events are proceeding as scheduled, so it’s recommended to check before your visit.

## Average Temperatures by Season, Clothing Tips, and Precautions in Tateyama Kurobe

![Live Camera View of Tateyama Kurobe](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2025/04/24-231947.webp)

The [official website](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/) also offers real-time camera feeds, so checking the weather conditions beforehand can help ensure a safer and more enjoyable trip!

The live images are divided into three areas: Murodo, Daikanbo, and Mida Plain.

### Spring (March to May)

**Temperature and Weather Characteristics**

\- Lower elevations (e.g., Kurobe Dam): Daytime around 10°C to 15°C, nighttime around 5°C.

\- Higher elevations (e.g., Murodo): Still cold with temperatures below 0°C, especially from March to April. Snow may not have fully melted, with lows reaching -10°C.

**Clothing Recommendations**

\- Lower elevations: Wear spring jackets, sweaters, and prepare warm accessories like scarves.

\- High elevations: Make sure to wear windproof and insulated down jackets, waterproof hiking shoes, and use slip-resistant gear on the snow walkways.

**Precautions**

\- The spectacular Snow Wall in the Great Snow Corridor often opens from mid-April to late June; check the official website for current conditions.

\- Spring can bring sudden snowstorms; allow flexible scheduling.

### Summer (June to August)

**Temperature and Weather Characteristics**

\- Lower elevations: Daytime temperatures around 20°C to 28°C, nights around 15°C.

\- Higher elevations (e.g., Murodo): Daytime around 18°C, nights dropping to about 5°C.

**Clothing Recommendations**

\- Wear lightweight long-sleeve shirts and athletic shoes.

\- Carry a light jacket for early mornings and evenings.

\- At high altitudes, still need to prepare windproof and warm clothing like lightweight down or fleece jackets.

**Precautions**

\- Summer is the best season for hiking; wear appropriate footwear for long walks and carry rain gear in case of afternoon showers.

\- The intense sunlight requires sun protection—apply sunscreen and wear hats.

### Autumn (September to November)

**Temperature and Weather Characteristics**

\- Lower elevations: Temperatures in September range from 15°C to 25°C, gradually dropping below 10°C from October to November.

\- High elevations (e.g., Murodo): Daytime temperatures below 10°C, nights near 0°C, with snow starting around November.

**Clothing Recommendations**

\- Bring autumn and winter outerwear, warm layers, and fleece or scarves, especially for high elevations.

\- Carry waterproof shoes and windproof clothing to handle sudden cold snaps and rain.

**Precautions**

\- From late September, the breathtaking maple leaf season begins. Visiting between mid-October and early November offers ideal scenery with red and gold foliage.

\- Late November, some trails may close due to winter conditions; check ahead.

### Winter (December to February)

**Temperature and Weather Characteristics**

\- Extremely cold: Daytime temperatures near -10°C to -15°C around Murodo, feeling even colder with wind chill.

\- Heavy snowfall in valleys and at low altitudes, with annual accumulations exceeding several meters.

**Clothing Recommendations**

\- Dress in full winter gear: down jackets, snow boots, wool hats, thick gloves, and windproof goggles.

\- Wear shoes with good grip to prevent slipping.

**Precautions**

\- Although access may be restricted in heavy snow, late December to February offers stunning snow scenery.

\- The area is popular for skiing and snow activities—perfect for capturing the winter wonderland.

\- Always check weather forecasts and transportation schedules in advance to ensure safe travel.

## Seasonal Activities in Tateyama Kurobe

![Tateyama Ropeway](https://resources.matcha-jp.com/resize/720x2000/2025/04/24-231950.webp)

### Recommended Activities in Spring

**Most Famous: Snow Wall Walkway Adventure**

From mid-April to late June, the Snow Wall (Yuki no Otani) is the top must-see spot. Visitors can walk between towering snow walls and experience the breathtaking winter scenery.

_Snow-scape photography from April to May:_ Use the high-altitude terrain to capture stunning scenes where snow and spring blossoms intermingle.

### Recommended Activities in Summer

**Lake Kurobe Sightseeing Cruise**

Visit during July to October to experience the most spectacular flood discharge of the Kurobe Dam.

**Highland Hiking & Cool Getaway**

Explore trails around Murodo and other highland areas, where the comfortable temperatures are perfect for outdoor adventures and escaping the heat.

### Recommended Activities in Autumn

**Autumn Foliage Viewing Tour**

October is the prime season to view the vibrant red and golden leaves. Riding cable cars and buses to high viewpoints offers panoramic vistas of the colorful mountain forests.

**Hot Spring Experience around Toyama**

After a stroll through the alpine forests, relax and unwind at local hot spring inns.

### Recommended Activities in Winter

**Snow Photography and Skiing**

With abundant snow, Tateyama Kurobe is a paradise for winter sports enthusiasts. Although the entire Alpen Route closes in winter, nearby ski resorts are conveniently accessible for snowboarding and skiing fun.

## Tips and Precautions for Visiting Tateyama Kurobe

**Transportation Arrangements:**

The Alpen Route requires multiple modes of transportation, such as cable cars and shuttle buses. It is recommended to purchase tickets in advance and check schedules to ensure smooth travel.

**Weather Variability**

Regardless of the season, temperatures on the mountain are significantly lower than at sea level. Be sure to pack layered clothing to adapt to sudden temperature changes.

**Check Operating Hours**

Cable cars, buses ( [link](https://willer-travel.com/en/?aid=462)), and attraction hours vary between peak and off-peak seasons. Always verify opening times beforehand to avoid missing out.

**Safety Precautions:**

Whether hiking or skiing, be sure to purchase travel insurance and equip yourself with safety gear.

## Enjoy Exploring Tateyama Kurobe

The Tateyama Kurobe area offers unique charm throughout all four seasons, making it a must-visit destination for first-time travelers in Japan. Whether enjoying the snow walls in spring, cooling off in summer, admiring autumn foliage, or capturing winter snow scenes, each season provides unforgettable experiences.

Prepare your luggage, plan your itinerary following the weather tips, clothing advice, and safety precautions outlined above! Enjoy exploring this dreamy mountain paradise comfortably and effortlessly.

Cherry blossoms, tulips, and many other flowers bloom beautifully in Toyama in April.

April also marks the opening of the Snow Wall Walk, a highlight of the Kurobe Tateyama Alpine Route.

The experience is available from mid-April to late June.

Temperatures in spring range from approximately 7°C to 21°C, so it's always a good idea to have a light jacket that you can throw on.

Late April to early May — Tonami Tulip Fair


Mid-April to late June — Snow Wall Walk

Hot and humid summers, daytime temperatures can exceed 30°C (86°F).

During this season, we recommend avoiding the heat at high altitude. The best season for climbing Tateyama is from July to August.

It is also a good time to attend nighttime festivals. The heat is less intense than during the day.

Whether sightseeing by the sea or climbing the mountain, hats and other sunshades are necessary.

The autumn foliage season is from September to October in the mountains and from October to November in the plains.

In October, snow may flicker near the top of Tateyama.

The Kurobe Gorge trolley car is in regular operation until mid-November, so don't miss the short autumn foliage season.

Temperatures range from 7℃ to 21℃. A jacket that is easy to put on and take off is useful.

Winter is the season for hot springs, snow lights, and seasonal seafood.

From late December to late February, mountainous areas are covered with snow.

In the Shogawa Gorge, the landscape looks like an ink painting, and in Gokayama, the Gassho-zukuri roofs are covered with snow.

January and February are cold, with temperatures ranging from 0°C to 7°C, so be sure to stay warm, but March is a bit milder.

Late December to late February — Shogawa Gorge Snowscape


Late December to late February — Gokoyama Snowscape


Early January to late March — Winter Wonderland in Unazuki Onsen: Fireworks over the Snow


November to February — Winter Seafood Season

The temperatures shown on this page are mainly for the plains.

Murodo, the highest point of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, located at an altitude of about 2450 m, has much lower temperatures than the graph, ranging from 5 to 10 degrees in April to June, 10 to 20 degrees in July and August, around 10 degrees in September and October, and sometimes below freezing in November.

Please note that the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is usually closed from December to mid-April.

web.markdown:
### Important Points for Your Stay #### Please read the following before your stay. - Hotel Tateyama is a built in a unique location that is 2,450 m above sea level.As the air pressure is low and the air thin, even healthy individuals may show symptoms of altitude sickness. - **Those with heart disease, high blood pressure and other chronic conditions as well as pregnant women and parents that plan to bring young children should take special care. Please discuss with your doctor and take health precautions before visiting us.** - If you take medication regularly, please do not forget to bring it with you. - If your condition worsens, the hotel will do what it can to assist you. However, we do not have a doctor or an ambulance on site. It will take time for emergency medical assistance to arrive. - **All rooms are non-smoking.**\[Smoking Areas\] \*For Hotel Tateyama guests \- Smoking area (3F large public bath) #### Hotel Tateyama is inaccessible by car. - Personal vehicles are not permitted on the route between the Tateyama and Ogizawa stations of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. - If you are visiting from the Tateyama side, please park your car at Tateyama Station and ride the cable car. - If you are visiting from the Shinano Omachi side, please park your car at Ogizawa Station and take the Kanden Tunnel Trolley Bus. [FAQ](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/en/information/faq.php) ### For customers using door-to-door delivery service #### Sending your baggage to Hotel Tateyama by mail Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is not part of the domestic mail route,(postal workers cannot drive here)so please send your baggage to the address below(all mailing services can be used). \*Outside of the round-trip delivery region #### Applicable Period For guests staying between April 15 – August 30th - **Kindly dispatch the goods four days prior to the scheduled date of accommodation. Due to the possibility of inclement weather and transportation disruptions, the date of arrival may fluctuate. (When sending luggage, please allow plenty of time for shipping, especially from April to mid-May.)** - Snow removal and road conditions may affect the date and time of the delivery of your baggage.Send your baggage no later than 4 days before your stay. - Contact the Hotel Tateyama front desk [（PHONE: 076-463-3345）](tel:076-463-3345) for all inquiries. #### Important Points - When sending your luggage, be sure to write the following on the notes section or the blank space of your luggage. **1\. Name of guest who made the reservation (For organizations, use the organization name. For groups, use the name of the group representative.)** **2\. Date(s) of your hotel stay** **3\. Luggage count** - Tateyama Kurobe Service Co., Ltd. does not any take inquiries regarding service. #### Sending Packages from the Hotel Deliveries (via Yu-Pack parcels) accepted at Hotel Tateyama Shop. Accepted through the morning of November 20th. ### Natural Environment #### Atmospheric pressure of 760 hPa (average value for Murodo) The atmospheric pressure down on level land is 1,013 hPa, meaning that Murodo's pressure is only 3/4 of that at sea level.This is why the potato chip bags in this picture look like inflated balloons.The air up here is thin, so you may find yourself running out of breath when climbing stairs or exerting yourself. Take your time, and move slowly. Because the atmospheric pressure is low, boiled water can only reach 92 degrees Celsius.You cannot make delicious rice using normal methods no matter how long you cook it here, which is why our hotel uses a special pressure cooker. ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information01.jpg) #### Temperature and snow depth The temperature in Murodo is 15 degrees Celsius lower than that at sea level. When it is 35 degrees Celsius in summer at sea level, it is only 20 degrees Celsius at Murodo, which feels more like springtime weather.Murodo has an average snow depth of 7–8 meters, and our snowdrifts can be 20 meters deep. [Clothing and personal belongings advice](https://www.alpen-route.com/information/advice_clothes.html) ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information02.jpg) #### Average temperature at Murodo-daira \*Average value from 2016 to 2025 | Date | Low

Approximately 3,000 Raicho inhabit Japan, with 250 – 300 birds inhabiting the 1070 ha of Murodo-daira, making it the country's most densely populated area for the bird. Mt. Tateyama's Raicho are not very afraid of people. It is said that this is because they are traditionallyknown as messengers of the gods and were treated kindly throughout the ages. 's most densely populated area for the bird. ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information04.jpg) #### Mt. Tateyama's glacier Yamasaki Cirque, a cirque valley created by long-term Ice Age erosion, can be found on Mt. Tateyama's west side.It is named after geographer Naomasa Yamasaki who discovered it in 1905 as evidence of Japan once having glaciers.It is one of Japan's special natural monuments. In recent years, Japan's first recognized existing glacier was discovered on Mt. Tateyama. A chunk of ice in the snowy valley on the south side of Mt. Oyama was discovered by GPS satellites to be a slow-moving glacier. Until recently, the glaciers on Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula were considered to be the world's southernmost glaciers, but that title now belongs to Mt. Tateyama's. ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information05.jpg) ### Nature conservation and Hotel Tateyama #### Building characteristics Hotel Tateyama is located in the Special Protection Area of the Chubu-Sangaku National Park, and was built adhering to the strict regulations pertaining to building location, size, height, exterior, and other factors to preserve the natural scenery. Construction began in 1968, and extreme difficulty was experienced during the process.After four years, Hotel Tateyama was completed on September 1, 1972.The cost of construction was three times that of a normal hotel. The building contains many thick pillars measuring over 10 meters to withstand snowfall. The outer walls contain many reinforced iron bars, and are much thicker than walls found in buildings at sea level.In order to prevent condensation building up from the extreme temperature difference inside and outside of the building, the inner rooms are built leaving a 30 centimeter space away from the outer concrete walls. ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information06.jpg) #### Management - **Electricity** Electricity is delivered to Hotel Tateyama by the Chuo Denryoku Kita-omachi Transformer Substation which sends the electricity via power line to Ogizawa. It then traverses the Kansai Electric Tunnel to reach Hokuriku Denryoku Kurobe Gozen Transformer Substation, where it takes the Tateyama Tunnel to arrive at Murodo. - **Water** The water used at Hotel Tateyama is Tateyama Tamadono Spring Water, sourced from the fault crushing belt in Tateyama Tunnel.The water contains a suitable amount of minerals, is preserved at around 4 degrees Celsius, and was chosen as one of the Top 100 Famous Spring Waters by the Ministry of the Environment. It is truly the miracle water of Mt. Tateyama.The mountain freezes over from winter to spring, making the spring water unavailable until it melts in late June. During the period, we use spring water from a separate source in Jigokudani.This is why we cannot offer Tateyama Tamadono Spring Water in the baths of all rooms at Hotel Tateyama. - **Heating** The central heating is on year-round, except during the 40 days of midsummer. Even when Hotel Tateyama is closed during the winter, rooms are kept at 5 degrees Celsius to prevent damage caused by the cold. ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information07.jpg) #### Caring for the environment In order to keep the environment free of wastewater as much as possible, some of the utensils used at Hotel Tateyama are not washed here, but instead sent to our company's dishwashing center at the foot of the mountain.Hotel Tateyama is also equipped with a combination water treatment basin for the purpose of releasing wastewater in a natural-like state. Ingredients used in food at Hotel Tateyama are processed at our distribution center at the foot of the mountain so that we produce very little raw garbage when cooking on the mountain. The small amount of raw garbage that is produced here is sent to a garbage compaction and drying facility to be compressed, and it is then not burnt, but sent to a public facility off of the mountain for processing. - **Take part in our Consecutive Stay No Cleaning Service** Hotel Tateyama is built at the altitude of 2,450 m, inside the Chubu Mountain National Park.We ask guests staying at Hotel Tateyama for two nights or more to help us lower our effect on the environment and reduce waste by taking part in our Consecutive Stay No Cleaning Service. Thank for you understanding and joining us to protect the Mt. Tateyama environment for future generations. Please inform the front desk if you do not wish to have your room cleaned or amenities replaced. ![](https://h-tateyama.alpen-route.co.jp/information/img/pt-information08.jpg) | | | | --- | --- | | | |

web.markdown:
Murodo (2,450m above sea level) on the Japan Alpine Route is about 2°C right after the April opening, around 18°C even at the height of summer, and drops below freezing before the November close. Based on the official 5-year average temperature data, here is a breakdown of the seasonal weather, clothing, altitude-based temperature gaps, and must-have items from April through November.

![Travelers walking the Murodo Snow Wall on the Japan Alpine Route, dressed in layers](https://tripmate.news/images/posts/tateyama-alpine-route-weather-clothing-01.jpg)Travelers walking the Murodo Snow Wall on the Japan Alpine Route

## Alpine Route Monthly Weather & Temperature

This is the 5-year average temperature data (2021-2025) measured on site by the Alpine Route operator (Tateyama Kurobe Kanko Co., Ltd.).

| Period | 9 AM / 1 PM Temp | Chance of No Rain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mid-April ❄️ Snow Wall opens | 1.8°C / 4.0°C | 58% |
| Late April ❄️ Golden Week | 5.5°C / 7.6°C | 76% |
| Early May ❄️ Snow Wall peak | 5.1°C / 7.6°C | 73% |
| Mid-May ❄️ Recommended | 7.9°C / 10.1°C | 75% |
| Late May ❄️ Snow Wall, later half | 7.7°C / 9.9°C | 75% |
| Early June ❄️ Snow Wall, final stretch | 9.2°C / 11.0°C | 77% |
| Mid-June 🌿 Early summer | 11.1°C / 13.1°C | 70% |
| Late June 🌧️ Rainy season begins | 12.4°C / 14.0°C | 63% |

| Mid-September 🍂 Foliage begins | 14.4°C / 15.8°C | 74% |
| Late September 🍁 Autumn foliage | 11.6°C / 13.8°C | 72% |
| Early October 🍁 Foliage peak | 9.6°C / 11.9°C | 69% |
| Mid-October 🍁 Foliage, later half | 7.1°C / 9.7°C | 72% |
| Late October ⛄ Sudden chill | 3.7°C / 7.2°C | 81% |
| Early November ⛄ Season's end | 2.3°C / 5.9°C | 71% |
| Mid-November ⛄ Below freezing | -0.8°C / 2.5°C | 70% |
| Late November ⛄ Just before closing | -2.6°C / 0.8°C | 57% |

※ Source: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route official, Past Weather (5-year average, 2021-2025)

※ "Chance of No Rain" is the average of the morning and afternoon figures from the "晴・曇の確率 (chance of clear/cloudy skies)" in the official Alpine Route data.

👉 [**\[Official\] Check the current Alpine Route weather**](https://www.alpen-route.com/weather/)

Since these temperatures are 5-year averages, the actual weather can vary a lot from year to year. On a clear afternoon it can be 3-5°C higher than the table shows, and on a day with strong rain and wind the felt temperature can drop below freezing.

## Season-by-Season Summary

**❄️ Snow Wall season (mid-April to early June)**

The best time to see the Snow Wall and still get good weather is mid- to late May. The Snow Wall is still tall enough, while the chance of no rain holds steady at 75%. Mid-April is the coldest, at 2-4°C, and also the least stable, with only a 58% chance of no rain.

**🌧️ Rainy season (late June to mid-July)**

The chance of no rain is 61-63%, the lowest of the year. It's best to avoid the Alpine Route during this time, or to keep your plans flexible so you can change the dates.

**☀️ Summer season (late July to August)**

Temperatures of 16-18°C and a 76-84% chance of no rain make this the most comfortable time. It's a great time to enjoy trekking around Mikurigaike Pond and the alpine scenery.

**🍁 Autumn foliage season (mid-September to mid-October)**

The colors start at Murodo first and then move down to Kurobedaira and Daikanbo. Early October is the foliage peak, with temperatures around 10-12°C, so you'll need autumn hiking clothes.

**⛄ Season's end (late October to November)**

From late October it gets cold quickly, reaching temperatures similar to just after the April opening. After mid-November it drops below freezing, and the season ends on November 30.

## Spring Snow Wall Season (Apr-Jun): Layering Is the Key

In the spring Snow Wall season, Murodo averages 5-8°C in the morning and 8-10°C in the afternoon. The numbers alone are similar to March-April in Seoul, but at 2,450m above sea level, wind, UV rays, and reflected glare off the snowfield make it feel different.

**Official Alpine Route guide (Apr-Jun):** Temperatures are low, around -5 to 10°C, but you'll warm up as you walk, so clothing with a front zipper or buttons that's easy to take off and put back on is convenient.

The key is layering. When you walk around Murodo it’s cold, but inside the transport it’s warm, and once you come down to the Kurobe Dam the temperature rises by more than 7°C. If you stick with a single outfit, you’ll be cold or hot somewhere along the way.

**Recommended layering for the spring Snow Wall season (Apr-Jun)**

When you walk around Murodo, wear all three layers; take off the outer layer at the Kurobe Dam or inside the transport.

| Layer | Item | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | Functional long-sleeve shirt (moisture-wicking, quick-dry) | Wicks away sweat |
| Mid | Fleece or lightweight down | Warmth |
| Outer | Windproof, waterproof jacket | Blocks wind, rain, and snow |
| Bottom | Long pants (stretch fabric recommended) | For snowy ground |
| Footwear | Waterproof trekking shoes or high-cut boots | Snowy, wet ground |
| Accessories | Gloves, knit cap, hand warmers | For the felt temperature |

**April vs. May vs. June: even within spring, they differ**

If you’re going right after the April opening, prepare as if for a real winter hike. From mid-May onward it goes above 10°C during the day, so there’s a bit more breathing room.

| Period | Afternoon temp | Feels like | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mid-April | 4.0°C | Like a December-January hike in Korea | Hand warmers, gloves essential |
| Mid-May | 10.1°C | Like a March hike in Korea | Fleece, windproof jacket recommended |
| Early June | 11.0°C | Like an April hike in Korea | A thin insulating layer needed |

![Recommended layering outfit for the May Murodo Snow Wall season on the Alpine Route](https://tripmate.news/images/posts/tateyama-alpine-route-weather-clothing-02.jpg)Recommended layering for the May Murodo Snow Wall season

## Watch the Altitude Temperature Gap: Over 7°C on the Same Day

The point people get wrong most often on an Alpine Route trip is the temperature difference by altitude. Even at the same time on the same day, Murodo (2,450m) and the Kurobe Dam (1,470m) have completely different temperatures.

**Kurobe Dam (1,470m) temperature comparison**

| Period (gap) | Murodo afternoon | Kurobe Dam afternoon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mid-May (7.2°C) | 10.1°C | 17.3°C |
| Late July (6.0°C) | 18.1°C | 24.1°C |
| Early October (5.8°C) | 11.9°C | 17.7°C |

➡️ In any season, there's a 6-7°C gap between Murodo and the Kurobe Dam.

**Based on May: temperature comparison from Tokyo to Murodo**

| Location / altitude | Mid-May afternoon temp |
| --- | --- |
| Tokyo (40m) | about 22-25°C |
| Nagano (362m) | about 20-23°C |
| Kurobe Dam (1,470m) | 17.3°C |
| Murodo (2,450m) | 10.1°C |

➡️ Leave Tokyo in short sleeves and you'll find a 15°C difference by the time you reach Murodo. Go without a jacket and you won't be able to properly enjoy yourself up on the Snow Wall.

**When to change clothes by altitude**

As you move along the Alpine Route, the key is to adjust your clothes each time the altitude changes. Keep a fleece, a windproof jacket, and gloves and a hat in your backpack, and the most efficient way is to pull them out and put them on as you climb higher.

| Section | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tokyo → Nagano | Spring clothes (long or short sleeves) |
| Nagano → Ogizawa | Keep as is |
| Ogizawa → Kurobe Dam | Take out the fleece |
| Kurobedaira → Murodo | Put on the windproof jacket |
| Murodo Snow Wall walk | Add gloves and a hat |
| Murodo → Tateyama Station (descent) | Gradually take layers off as you go down |
| Tateyama Station → Toyama | Back to spring clothes |

## Summer & Autumn Clothing

### Summer (Jul-Aug): Short Sleeves, but an Outer Layer Is a Must

Murodo’s summer temperature is a comfortable 15-18°C in the afternoon, a cool retreat. When Tokyo is 35°C, Murodo is 18°C.

**Official Alpine Route guide (Jul-Aug):** The UV in the mountains is stronger than you'd expect, so clothing with less skin exposure is better. Even if it's clear in the morning, fog can suddenly roll in or showers can fall in the afternoon, dropping the temperature sharply.

In summer, alpine treks around Mikurigaike Pond and Raichozawa are popular. The trails are well maintained, but be sure to keep a rain poncho or windproof jacket in your backpack for the afternoon showers.

| Layer | Item | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | Short sleeves or thin long sleeves | Long sleeves recommended to block UV |
| Outer | Windproof jacket or rain poncho | For sudden afternoon changes, folded into your backpack |
| Bottom | Long pants | Shorts leave you exposed to UV and insects |
| Footwear | Trekking shoes | Trails are maintained but have ups and downs |

### Autumn (Sep-Oct): Foliage Season, Spring-Level Warmth

Autumn temperatures drop quickly. Early October is almost the same as mid-May. If you’re going to see the foliage in October, prepare the same layering as the spring Snow Wall season. From mid-October onward, you’ll also need hand warmers, gloves, and a knit cap.

### Season’s End (November): Full Winter Gear

In mid-November, the morning is -0.8°C, and in late November it’s -2.6°C. During this period you need winter hiking clothes. From November 4 a separate timetable applies, and the season ends on November 30.

![Comparison of summer and autumn seasonal clothing on the Japan Alpine Route](https://tripmate.news/images/posts/tateyama-alpine-route-weather-clothing-03.jpg)Summer and autumn clothing comparison by season on the Japan Alpine Route ( [Image source](https://www.alpen-route.com/index.php))

## Seasonal Packing Checklist

**Common to all seasons**

| Item | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Windproof, waterproof jacket | For wind, rain, and sudden temperature drops |
| Sunglasses | High-altitude UV + glare off the snowfield (listed as a "must-have" in the official guide) |
| Sunscreen (SPF50+) | UV at 2,450m is stronger than on flat ground |
| Waterproof trekking shoes | For snowy, wet ground and trails (high-cut recommended for Apr-Jun) |
| Spare camera battery / power bank | Batteries drain fast in the cold |
| Cash | There are no ATMs along the route, so bring small cash for shops and restaurants |
| Rain poncho or folding umbrella | For sudden changes in mountain weather |

**Additional items by season**

| Season | Fleece / lightweight down / cap | Gloves / hand warmers / neck warmer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apr-May | ⭕️ | ⭕️ |
| June | ⭕️ | ❌ |
| Jul-Aug | ❌ | ❌ |
| Sep-early Oct | ⭕️ | ❌ |
| Late Oct-Nov | ⭕️ | ⭕️ |

**⛔ Things to note**

- **Pets:** This is a special protection area of the Chubu Sangaku National Park, so all pets, including those in cages, are prohibited. (Only guide dogs are exempt.)
- **Drones:** Drone use along the Alpine Route is prohibited for flying, filming, and operating alike.

The key to dressing for the Alpine Route is to think differently than you would for Tokyo.

When Tokyo is 25°C in May, Murodo is 10°C. When Tokyo is 35°C in August, Murodo is 18°C. In late October, Murodo is 3.7°C in the morning, similar to just after the April opening.

Whatever the season, always pack one windproof jacket in your backpack.

Currently, all of them are summer trails.

The hiking trails around Murodo, Oyama, Jodōyama, and Ryūōdake are walked several times a week and are in good condition without any collapses.

The hiking trail repairs between Ichinokoshi and Harai-dō have already been completed, and the trail is currently passable without any issues.

## Mountaineering equipment

The basic equipment for autumn hiking in 3000-meter-class mountains.

The ridgeline is exposed and there are no places to hide, so you need to take measures against getting wet and wind with rainwear and jackets.

Gloves are also necessary.

If you come to the mountains with the mindset of the lowlands, you will end up walking while shivering.

As the wind blows, there are increasing days when the perceived temperature drops below freezing, so please be careful.

## Points to note

The daylight hours have become shorter.

Please make plans that allow for actions with ample time.

Oyama Shrine has closed for the season.

Please note that the restroom at the summit is also out of service.

It is also important to know when to retreat on site.

When entering the mountains, please check the weather on the day of your trip in advance.

[Toyama Prefecture / Northern Hida Mountain Range\\
**Mt. Tateyama Elevation: 3,015m**\\
Usually, when people say Mt. Tateyama , they are referring to either Mt. Oyama (3003m), which enshrines Oyama Shrine, or the three Mt. Tateyama mountains, including Jodosan, Oyama, and Betsuyama. In the past, Mt. Tateyama was used to include the three mountains of Kekatsu through to Mt. Yakushi , and in the Edo period literati painter Tani Buncho's "Illustrated Guide to Famous Mountains of Japan," Betsuyama, Mt. Tateyama , and Mt. Tsurugi are all referred to as " Mt. Tateyama ." In other words, it is a vague mountain range.\\
The highest peak in that area is Mount Oyama. It is thought to have been the inner shrine of Oyama Shrine, as it was historically referred to as 'Mikunaijin'. It towers slightly to the east of the traverse route.\\
Mount Oyama, composed of granite and green schist gneiss, has a cirque known as a glacial landform on its western side. Named after Yamasaki Naohō, a pioneer in Japanese geography who first discovered Japan's glacial landforms, Yamasaki Cirque has been designated as a natural monument.\\
Due to heavy snowfall on the eastern side of the mountain caused by the northwest seasonal winds in winter, most of Japan's cirque formations have developed on eastern slopes, making the Yamasaki Cirque on the western slope rare. It can be viewed from Murodō.\\
The land registry is Mt. Tateyama Town, Nakaniikawa District, Toyama Prefecture. It is a volcano that belongs to the Norikura volcanic belt, and stands on the lava plateau of Midagahara. Another face of Mt. Tateyama is that, along with Mt. Haku in Kaga, it has long been worshiped as a sacred mountain in the Hokuriku region and is a mountain of Shugendo.\\
The mountain was opened in the first year of Taiho (701) when Saeki Yorai of Ecchu (Jikyo Shonin), while hunting, pursued a wounded bear into the deep mountains and cornered it in a rock cave. Upon entering, the bear transformed into Amida Nyorai and Fudo Myoo, commanding the "opening of Mt. Tateyama." In the same 8th century, the Manyo poet Otomo no Yakamochi, who was appointed governor of Ecchu Province, sang, "Even in the eternal summer, I never tire of seeing the snow that falls on Mt. Tateyama; it must be a divine land." Thus, Mt. Tateyama is a mountain filled with spiritual power.\\
In later years, it became a training center for the Tendai sect and the Shingon esoteric Buddhism, and the unique philosophy of likening the three mountains of Mt. Tateyama Mt. Tateyama to paradise and Jigokudani and Mt. Tsurugi to hell gave birth to the Mt. Tateyama sect, and the number of believers increased through nationwide evangelism using the visual appeal of the Mt. Tateyama mandala paintings by the monks of Ashikura-ji Temple at the foot of the mountain. In particular, the selling point was the "Nunobashi Daikanjo" ceremony, which claimed that women could go to paradise, which was a religious taboo, and it was a banner of advanced and spiritual women's liberation in the Edo period.\\
The surprise and joy of hearing sermons accompanied by illustrations preaching about hell and paradise, and about how even women could attain rebirth in paradise, something that is impossible in other sects, created a buzz among Mt. Tateyama followers, who turned the ascetic efforts of the 30-odd kilometres of mountain trails from Ashikuraji up Zaimokuzaka and along the vast Midagahara plain to Murodo and Mt. Oyama into pleasure.\\
Current hikers transfer by cable car or bus to Murodo, reach Oyama in 2 hours and 30 minutes from Murodo, and then climb to the highest peak, Onanji Mountain, in an additional 15 minutes.](https://www.yamakei-online.com/yamanavi/yama.php?yama_id=502)

[Toyama Prefecture / Northern Hida Mountain Range\\
**Okudainichidake Altitude 2,611m**\\
It is a little inconspicuous because it is located in the same mountain range as theMt. Tateyamamountain range, but the figure from Mitabahara and Murodohira is large and heavy.\\
Mt. TateyamaAt the highest peak of the Dainichi Ridge, which branches west at Tsurugigozen on the main ridge connecting Sanzan andMt. Tsurugi, descends to Shinmurodo Nori-Etsu, and then undulates.\\
As you can see from the name Dainichi, this is also a mountain of Shugen, and as a vanguard peak of the spiritual peakMt. Tateyama, it was a sacred place for the embodiment of Dainichi Nyorai. From here, the majestic view ofMt. Tsurugiover the deep valley of theMt. TateyamaRiver is stunning, and a view worthy of a place of worship.\\
Up to this point, the Dainichi Ridge consists of the same diorite as Mt. Tsurugi, but beyond here, it transitions to bright, younger granite. Thanks to the gentle shape of the mountains, there are many alpine meadows, and beautiful clusters of Hakusan ichige, Aleutian avens, Miyama daikonso, black lilies, and Kobai keisou can be seen among the dwarf pines.\\
The general hiking course starts from the end point of the Alpine Route at Murodo, crosses the Jodo River, climbs to Shin-Murodo Pass, and heads west along the Dainichi Ridge, taking 3 hours. Another route, mainly used for descent, is the Shomyozaka course, which goes from Shomyo-daira to Dainichi-daira, passes through Chudainichidake, and reaches the summit, taking 7 hours of steep climbing.](https://www.yamakei-online.com/yamanavi/yama.php?yama_id=499)

![Best Things to Do](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/1wx0o12000e50hgeo3091.png)No. 1 of Best Things to Do in Toyama Prefecture

Mountain climbing

Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route stretches across the Northern Alps peaks on the border of Toyama and Nagano prefectures. With multiple 3,000m-class peaks like Oyama, Onanji-yama, and Mount Tsurugi forming a continuous ridge, it represents the essence of the Japanese Alps scenery. Together with Mount Fuji and Mount Haku, it is known as one of Japan's three sacred mountains and has been a site of mountain worship for over a thousand years. Besides hiking, you can explore this area by using a relay of various transportation modes such as funiculars, highland buses, tunnel trolley buses, and ropeways to ascend from the mountain foot to above the sea of clouds.
Every spring, the Yuki no Ōtani section's snow walls can reach nearly 20m in height, making driving through it feel like passing through a white canyon; in summer and fall, alpine plants in the Midagahara wetlands bloom in succession and later turn into golden autumn colors. Sometimes, you may even encounter ptarmigans inhabiting the mountains. Murododaira, at an altitude of approx. 2,450m, is a plateau above the clouds. On sunny days, the nearby volcanic lake, Mikurigaike, reflects the Mount Tate peaks, making it a classic photo attraction; descending to the Kurobe River valley, the Kurobe Dam, standing over 180m tall, spans the deep valley. When water is discharged, the mist rises, creating an awe-inspiring sight; on the side of the mountain foot, the four-tiered Shomyo Falls, with a total drop of approx. 350m, is also worth a visit along the way.

- ### 🍁🏔️ Autumn on Japan’s Alpine Route — a journey through the Japanese Alps



If you want to experience autumn on a much grander scale, the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is one of the most spectacular journeys in Japan.

Instead of seeing autumn foliage from a single viewpoint, you travel through the mountains, crossing different elevations by cable car, ropeway, bus and on foot. 🚡🏔️

As you climb higher, the scenery keeps changing:

🍂 Lower elevations — forests turn red, orange and golden.
🏔️ Higher elevations — rugged alpine peaks appear, with crisp blue skies and dramatic mountain landscapes.
💧 Kurobe Dam — one of the highlights, where the massive dam and surrounding mountains create an incredible autumn panorama.

One of the most fascinating things about the Alpine Route is that autumn arrives at different times depending on altitude. So while the valleys may still be green, higher areas can already be glowing with autumn colors.

It feels less like visiting an autumn spot and more like travelling through an entire season in one day. 🍁✨

📍 Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, Toyama–Nagano, Japan

- ### A Magical Experience at Tateyama Kurobe



Tateyama Kurobe is the nickname for the 'Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route,' a road connecting 'Tateyama' Station in Tateyama Town, Toyama Prefecture, and 'Ogizawa' Station in Omachi City, Nagano Prefecture.
The route is 37.2 kilometers long, with the highest point at an altitude of 2,450 meters and a maximum elevation difference of 2,000 meters. It is a famous mountain sightseeing route representing Japan and even the world. It is open to tourists for climbing from mid-April to mid-November each year.
